questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to the Bactrian camel, consider the following statements:
1. It has two humps that store fat.
2. In India it is found in the Nubra Valley of Ladakh.
3. The wild Bactrian camel (Camelus ferus) is listed as Endangered by the IUCN.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. About 300-400 Bactrian camels are found in India. The domesticated Bactrian camel is not considered a threatened species.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to stingless bees, consider the following statements:
1. Amazon's stingless bees have become the first insect to be granted legal rights.
2. Their stingers are fully functional and are used for defence.
3. They belong to the world's oldest bee lineage, existing for nearly 80 million years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Their stingers are highly reduced and functionally useless for defence. Nearly 500 species exist globally, with over 170 in Peru, and they sustain about 80% of Amazonian flora.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to freshwater pufferfish, consider the following statements:
1. They are a group of about 30 to 35 species in the family Tetraodontidae that live their entire lives in fresh water.
2. They are found in the Western Ghats and in basins such as the Ganga, Brahmaputra and Mahanadi.
3. Their poison, tetrodotoxin, is a mild toxin of little danger to humans.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Tetrodotoxin (TTX) is one of the most potent neurotoxins known in nature. Pufferfish are omnivorous and live near the bottom. Scientists have confirmed India's first case of pufferfish poisoning.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to mycorrhizal networks, consider the following statements:
1. They are underground fungal networks that connect the roots of several plants through hyphae.
2. In the association, plants give carbohydrates to the fungi and receive better access to water and nutrients.
3. The network is popularly called the 'Wood Wide Web'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Tyler Prize, called the 'Nobel for the environment', was awarded to an American biologist for her work on these networks, which draw down about 13 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide into soil systems every year.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to bio-bitumen, consider the following statements:
1. It is made from organic materials such as agricultural waste, lignin, bio-char and bio-oil.
2. It can be used as an addition to bitumen or to reduce the amount of bitumen in the binder mixture.
3. India has become the first country to produce it commercially for road construction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. It can reduce crude oil imports and help address stubble burning. Ordinary bitumen is a black, adhesive substance produced by distilling crude oil.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Biomaterials are best described as materials that are:
opts: Made from crude oil that is processed so that it can be broken down by sunlight
Derived wholly or partly from living sources or made by biological steps
Produced only from minerals found underground in the form of metals and alloys
Made from plastics that are recycled and mixed with a small fraction of metals
questions.why: They offer sustainable alternatives to traditional petroleum-based products, with applications in biomedicine, packaging, agriculture, healthcare and textiles.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to youth in India, consider the following statements:
1. National Youth Day is observed on 12 January, the birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda.
2. The Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue 2026 was held in New Delhi.
3. The Agnipath Scheme recruits youth as 'Agniveers' to provide them with technical skills and discipline.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. India has the largest youth population in the world, with about 50% under 25 years of age and 65% under 35. The draft National Youth Policy 2025 sets a ten-year vision.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan (VBSA) Bill, 2025, consider the following statements:
1. The VBSA will control the funding of institutions.
2. It creates a unified regulatory architecture for higher education under Entry 66 of the Union List.
3. It repeals the University Grants Commission Act, 1956, the AICTE Act, 1987 and the NCTE Act, 1993.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The VBSA will not control the funding of institutions. Legal and medical education are exempted and will continue under separate Acts. The Bill was referred to a joint parliamentary committee.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the VBSA Bill, 2025, consider the following statements:
1. Viksit Bharat Shiksha Viniyaman Parishad is the council for regulation.
2. Viksit Bharat Shiksha Gunvatta Parishad is the council for accreditation.
3. Viksit Bharat Shiksha Manak Parishad is the council for academic standards.
4. Appeals against the decisions of the Commission and the Councils lie before the Supreme Court.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: Appeals against the decisions of the Commission and the Councils lie before the Central Government. A Council of Architecture is to be set up under the Architects Act, 1972, as a professional standard-setting body.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the regulation of higher education in India, consider the following statements:
1. Education is in the Concurrent List.
2. The National Board of Accreditation accredits colleges and universities as a whole.
3. Technical and scientific institutions, research and standards are in the Union List.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The NAAC, set up by the UGC, assesses colleges and universities on quality, while the NBA, under the AICTE Act, accredits specific technical programmes such as B.Tech in Mechanical Engineering.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Supreme Court's judgment in Amit Kumar v. Union of India on student suicides, consider the following statements:
1. Vacant faculty and administrative posts must be filled within a year.
2. The Court invoked Article 142 to address the rise in student suicides in higher educational institutions.
3. Institutions must report any suicide or unnatural death to the police immediately, wherever it occurs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Vacant faculty and administrative posts must be filled within four months, with priority for reserved categories. A National Task Force is to create a framework and model SOPs for well-being audits.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Supreme Court's observation on menstrual health in schools, consider the following statements:
1. The Court held that the right to life under Article 21 includes the right to menstrual health.
2. The Court linked the matter only to Article 19 and not to Article 21A.
3. The Court directed pan-India implementation of the Menstrual Hygiene Policy for School-going Girls for Classes 6-12.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Court also linked it to Article 14 and to the right to education under Article 21A. Schools must provide gender-segregated toilets, free sanitary napkins and dedicated menstrual hygiene management corners.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: 'Demographic Winter' is best described as a phase of:
opts: A temporary fall in births that is caused only by severe cold weather in some regions
A rapid rise in the share of young people that is caused by a high fertility rate
A fall in the death rate that results in a quick increase in the working-age group
A persistent, structural fall in population growth, with fertility below replacement
questions.why: The replacement fertility rate is 2.1. China's population fell for the fourth consecutive year, by 3.39 million to 1.405 billion, with 7.92 million births in 2025.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the scramjet engine, consider the following statements:
1. It operates efficiently at hypersonic speeds above Mach 5 and allows supersonic combustion.
2. It has no mechanical compressor or turbine.
3. It can produce thrust from zero air speed without assistance from another propulsion system.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Ramjets and scramjets cannot produce thrust at zero air speed, so they need a rocket or turbojet to reach a high enough speed. India is the fourth country to demonstrate flight testing of a scramjet, after the US, Russia and China.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: A scramjet engine differs from a rocket engine in that the scramjet:
opts: Uses oxygen from the atmospheric air as the oxidiser instead of carrying its own
Carries both the fuel and the oxidiser in tanks inside the vehicle to burn in a chamber
Uses a rotating mechanical compressor and turbine to compress the incoming air flow
Works in space where there is no air, by using a gas that is stored on the vehicle
questions.why: A scramjet generally uses hydrogen as fuel. It is more efficient than a rocket, which carries both fuel and oxidiser.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the PSLV-C62 / EOS-N1 mission, consider the following statements:
1. It was a successful mission with no anomaly.
2. It was the 64th flight of the PSLV.
3. It was the ninth dedicated commercial mission of NSIL.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The mission encountered an anomaly during the third stage. NSIL, incorporated in 2019, is the commercial arm of ISRO and is wholly owned by the Government under the Department of Space.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the PSLV, consider the following statements:
1. It is a third-generation launch vehicle and the first Indian launch vehicle with liquid stages.
2. Its second stage uses the Vikas engine.
3. Its first stage uses the S139 solid rocket motor with six strap-on boosters.
4. In 2017 it launched 10 satellites in a single mission.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: In 2017 the PSLV launched 104 satellites in a single mission, a world record. It can carry up to 1,750 kg to Sun-synchronous polar orbits of 600 km.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to India's first private Earth observation constellation, consider the following statements:
1. A Pixxel-led consortium signed an agreement with IN-SPACe.
2. It is a fully government-built and government-operated infrastructure.
3. It will consist of 12 satellites, including optical, multispectral, SAR and hyperspectral imaging.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It is a Public-Private Partnership, a shift from government-built to industry-operated national Earth observation infrastructure, with an investment of Rs 1,200 crore over five years. IN-SPACe is the nodal agency that authorises, regulates and promotes private participation in space.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to dark matter, consider the following statements:
1. It makes up about 68% of the universe.
2. It does not emit, absorb or reflect light.
3. Its existence is inferred from its gravitational effects on ordinary matter.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Dark matter makes up about 27% of the universe and dark energy about 68%, while normal matter is about 5%. Astronomers have unveiled a detailed map of dark matter based on James Webb Space Telescope observations.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the Fourth Industrial Revolution, consider the following statements:
1. The term was coined by Klaus Schwab, the founder of the World Economic Forum, in 2016.
2. The WEF centre announced for Andhra Pradesh will be the first such centre in India.
3. It describes the convergence of digital, physical and biological technologies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It will be the third such centre in India, after Mumbai and Telangana. The IMF says almost 40% of global employment is exposed to AI.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the Battery Pack Aadhaar Number (BPAN), consider the following statements:
1. It is an indigenous system for end-to-end traceability of batteries through their life cycle.
2. It gives each battery pack a unique identification number.
3. It is required for all batteries, including those in small consumer products.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Draft guidelines require electric vehicle batteries and industrial batteries with capacity above 2 kWh to keep a BPAN as an electronic record. It helps second-life use and recycling.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication does not rely on third-party networks such as cellular networks.
Statement-II: V2V communication can help vehicles share warnings even when a hazard is not visible, strengthening Advanced Driver Assistance Systems.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
opts: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.why: Both are correct, but one does not explain the other. It works across the front, rear and sides of vehicles and factors in terrain and road curves.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: The Mpemba effect refers to the observation that:
opts: Under certain conditions, colder substances can boil sooner than the hotter ones do
Under all conditions, ice melts at a higher temperature than the pure water freezes
Under certain conditions, hotter substances can freeze faster than colder ones
Under certain conditions, salt water freezes at a higher temperature than pure water
questions.why: It is most famously seen in water but is not limited to it. It matters for heat engines, refrigeration, quantum computing and materials science.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the Nipah virus, consider the following statements:
1. It was first identified in an outbreak in India in 2018.
2. It is a zoonotic virus whose natural reservoir is fruit bats.
3. It can spread to humans through raw date palm sap or fruit contaminated by bats.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It was first identified in a 1999 outbreak in Malaysia and Singapore, in which it passed from bats to pigs to humans. The incubation period is 4 to 14 days.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to staphylococci, consider the following statements:
1. They are gram-positive cocci that occur in clusters.
2. They are viruses.
3. Staphylococcus aureus and Staphylococcus epidermidis are the main types.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: They are bacteria. Researchers found high levels of antibiotic-resistant staphylococci in indoor and outdoor air in parts of Delhi.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Somnath Temple, consider the following statements:
1. The present temple is built in the Dravida style.
2. It is located at Prabhas Patan near Veraval in Gujarat.
3. It is revered as the first among the twelve Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The present temple is in the Maru-Gurjara (Chalukya or Solanki) style. Its 'Kailash Mahameru Prasad' form has a garbhagriha, a sabhamandap and a nrityamandap, and a 150-foot shikhar.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the history of the Somnath Temple, consider the following statements:
1. Mahmud of Ghazni raided it in 1026, during the reign of Bhima I.
2. Ahilyabai Holkar rebuilt the temple in the 18th century.
3. The present temple was inaugurated by President Rajendra Prasad on 11 May 1951.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The temple was destroyed again in 1297, 1394 and 1706, and was looted as many as 17 times. Its post-independence reconstruction was initiated by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: Which one of the following writers recorded the destruction of the Somnath temple by the army of Alauddin Khilji in the 13th century?
opts: Al-Biruni, in the Kitab-al-Hind written in the eleventh century
Kalidasa, in the Raghuvamsa written in the fifth century
Abul Fazl, in the Ain-i-Akbari written in the sixteenth century
questions.why: Al-Biruni praised the temple in the 11th century, and Kalidasa mentioned Somnath-Prabhasa as a Shiva pilgrimage site in the 5th century.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to Maru-Gurjara architecture, consider the following statements:
1. It originated in the 6th century in the regions of Rajasthan and Gujarat.
2. It reached its peak under the Chalukya (Solanki) dynasty of Gujarat.
3. A jharokha is a projecting stone window or suspended balcony.
4. A jaali is a rain-water storage tank across a slope.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: A jaali is a perforated stone or latticed screen with geometric or calligraphic patterns. A johad is a rain-water storage tank or barrier built across slopes to replenish groundwater.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Padma Awards, consider the following statements:
1. They are conferred in three categories: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri.
2. The awards do not amount to a title under Article 18(1) and cannot be used as a prefix or suffix.
3. The number of awards is capped at 120 a year, excluding posthumous and foreigner awards.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Government servants are not eligible, except doctors and scientists. The Balaji Raghavan v. Union of India (1996) judgment dealt with the status of the awards.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to gallantry awards in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Param Vir Chakra is the highest military decoration for the most conspicuous bravery.
2. The Param Vir Chakra, Maha Vir Chakra and Vir Chakra were instituted in 1952.
3. The Ashoka Chakra is the highest peacetime award for bravery away from the battlefield.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The wartime awards were instituted on 26 January 1950, and the peacetime awards on 4 January 1952, renamed in 1967 as the Ashoka Chakra, Kirti Chakra and Shaurya Chakra. They are conferred by the President.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Bhadrakali inscription, consider the following statements:
1. It is a 12th-century inscription embedded in the wall of the Bhadrakali Temple at Prabhas Patan, Gujarat.
2. It is a prashasti of Acharya Bhavabrihaspati, the spiritual preceptor of the Solanki king Kumarapala.
3. It records that the Somnath Temple was built only in stone from the beginning.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The inscription is dated to 1169 CE. It gives a legendary history of the Somnath Temple across the four Yugas, mentioning its construction in gold, silver and wood, and finally in stone by Bhimdev Solanki.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Zehanpora site in Baramulla, Kashmir, consider the following statements:
1. The finds show that Kashmir had no Buddhist heritage.
2. The stupa structures there belong to the Kushan period.
3. It lies along the ancient Silk Route to Kandahar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The discovery underscores Kashmir's Gandhara Buddhist heritage and its role as a centre of Buddhist culture and learning. Other finds include wooden superstructures, Kushan-era pottery and copper artefacts.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Bagurumba dance, consider the following statements:
1. It is a traditional folk dance of the Bodo community of Assam.
2. It is a classical dance form of Odisha.
3. It is traditionally performed by young Bodo women, with men accompanying as musicians.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It is inspired by nature and symbolises blooming flowers. It is associated with festivals such as Bwisagu, the Bodo New Year, and Domasi.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q:
Consider the following harvest festivals and the States with which they are associated in the news:
1. Pongal : Tamil Nadu
2. Lohri : Punjab
3. Magh Bihu : Assam
4. Kanuma : Karnataka
How many of the above are correctly matched?
questions.why: Kanuma is celebrated in Telangana. Magh Bihu marks the end of the harvest season with community feasts and bonfires called Meji, and Lohri is celebrated a day before Makar Sankranti.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: Uttarayana, known for kite flying, is a harvest festival celebrated mainly in which of the following?
questions.why: These festivals mark the change of seasons, the Sun's northward journey (Uttarayana) and the harvest of crops. Makar Sankranti marks the Sun's transition into Capricorn.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the regulation of AI on social media in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 does not apply to platforms that control AI systems.
2. The IT Act, 2000 and the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 form the backbone of social media regulation.
3. Non-compliance can lead to loss of safe harbour protection under Section 79 of the IT Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The DPDP Act, 2023 requires data fiduciaries, including platforms that control AI systems, to comply with prior consent, data protection measures and grievance redressal. The POCSO Act and the Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act make it illegal to create or share obscene material.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the governance of artificial intelligence, consider the following statements:
1. MeitY issued the India AI Governance Guidelines, which present seven sutras for ethical AI governance.
2. The EU Act allows AI practices that involve subliminal manipulation of users.
3. The EU Artificial Intelligence Act, agreed in 2024, is described as the world's first comprehensive AI law.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The EU Act categorises AI systems by risk and prohibits unacceptable-risk practices such as subliminal manipulation. OECD and UNESCO principles are non-binding but press companies to uphold fairness, transparency, privacy and human oversight.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Atal Pension Yojana (APY), consider the following statements:
1. It was launched in 2015 and is implemented by PFRDA under the National Pension System.
2. It is open to bank account holders aged 18 to 40 who are not income tax payers.
3. It guarantees a lifelong monthly pension of Rs 10,000 to Rs 25,000 from age 60.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The guaranteed monthly pension is between Rs 1,000 and Rs 5,000. The Union Cabinet approved its continuation until 2030-31, and over 8.66 crore subscribers had enrolled by 19 January 2026.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Atal Pension Yojana, consider the following statements:
1. It is a Central Sector Scheme under the Ministry of Finance.
2. On the death of the subscriber, the spouse receives the pension and the nominee receives the corpus.
3. The Government co-contribution was for subscribers who joined between 1 June 2015 and 31 March 2016.
4. A voluntary exit before age 60 returns the contribution along with the Government's co-contribution.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.why: On a voluntary exit the subscriber receives only the contribution with interest, and the Government co-contribution is forfeited. The co-contribution was 50% of the total contribution or Rs 1,000 a year, whichever was lower, for five years.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to PM Street Vendors AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi), consider the following statements:
1. It is a Central Sector Scheme launched in 2020 by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
2. It provides collateral-free working capital loans to street vendors.
3. Street vendors are now eligible for a dedicated credit card with a limit of up to Rs 30,000.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The loan tranches are Rs 15,000, Rs 25,000 and Rs 50,000, and there is a 7% interest subsidy for timely repayment and up to Rs 1,600 in cashback for digital transactions.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The credit guarantee cover for loans under PM SVANidhi is administered by:
opts: The National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company for startups and small firms
The Small Industries Development Bank of India as its parent organisation
The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development in its rural wing
The Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises
questions.why: The scheme is implemented jointly by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and the Department of Financial Services. States must have notified rules under the Street Vendors Act, 2014.
